newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen rising with higher volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen rising with higher volume.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to push higher at the opening Friday, fuelled by stronger volume after a drop in U.S. long bond yields, dealers said.

"The U.S. bonds market was soothed by statements by (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan, pushing the yield to its lowest level in the week, and this should rub off on the bolsa," one trader said.
Greenspan said in a speech at New York University Thursday night that he saw scant signs of a resurgence of inflation and expected the economy to slow later in the year and into 1998.
His words rekindled debate over whether the Fed will hike rates again when its Open Market Committee meets May 20.
"Until now a May 20 rate hike was pretty much a foregone conclusion. Now we're starting to wonder about it again," the trader said.
The blue-chip MerVal index added 0.3 percent to 726.62 Thursday, paring losses in the week to 0.8 percent.

Some traders were only cautiously optimistic, noting the market was still digesting company results and waiting for news from the domestic front, including details of the planned $3.0 billion sale of the National Mortgage Bank.
"We want to see if the windfalls are used in a sensible manner or with electoral aims," said Norman Trabucco at Zaracan traders, in reference to October's mid-term elections.
"The bolsa is firm and while company results have been in line with expectations, it's not possible yet to break a trading range of 710-740," the broker added.
